segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Let's talk about the physical material that you've been involved in analyzing with Professor Garry Nolan. You've spent decades recovering and testing physical samples, and Forbidden Science 7 records the fact that the Trinity bracket, the bracket from the alleged Trinity craft, showed no signs of advanced technology. After all the alleged UFO/UAP material that you've tested, is there any one sample that you've personally tested that you do accept is genuinely non-human?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I think there is a misunderstanding about that. The composition of some of those is strange, but you could do it in the lab, you could do it in a high school lab. So the question is what about the structure of the molecules and the atoms — and that's a whole different problem. It's much more difficult, much more expensive. But some of that has been done. Some of that was done at Stanford by Professor Peter A. Sturrock. As you may know, I worked with Professor Sturrock in astrophysics at Stanford in the late 1960s and early 1970s, and then he donated his samples to me. So some of these come from him, and then I worked on them with different labs. I'm not capable of doing that analysis myself, I don't have access to those machines — it takes specialized engineers just to calibrate them and run them — but I know where they are. So I've done some of that and we've published some of them.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: The composition is bizarre, it's strange, we don't see what it matches. But even if we found that the isotopes have been manipulated, that doesn't mean… If you go to Mars and you find some minerals and you do this, you'll find isotope compositions that are similar to the Earth. It's given by the atomic structure, and that can change by a few percent, but it's not going to change by 30%. So if it changes by more than a few percent, somebody has done that. And of course we do that in medicine, with special things that are injected in the body for a particular reason and only stay in the body for 24 hours or something like that, and that's very, very expensive. What I can say is that some of the samples we could not manufacture for $100 million. Now, we do some of that for atomic fuel, of course — we've done that since the 1940s for the bomb, so we do that with uranium, we do that with fissile materials for nuclear weapons, where they have billions of dollars, not me. But this is not at the level of what we recover after a UFO observation.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Let's come to crash retrievals, then. You're very conservative on the subject of crash retrievals, although you do give credence to the Trinity case, which does appear to be a crash retrieval. Eric Davis tells you in Forbidden Science 7 that there is an ongoing crash retrieval program. And you talk in the book about an attempted AARO and Redstone briefing concerning a legacy crash retrieval program, and you write that Eric may know considerably more than Sean Kirkpatrick, the head of the Pentagon's UFO office at the time. And later on, Eric tells you that the program is a waived unacknowledged special access program involving recovered craft. You say the explanation clears the smoke around the disclosure issue — but what do you personally think? Do you accept that there are recovered non-human craft in the possession of the US government?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yes. As you know, I've spent a lot of time in New Mexico with specialists, with people from NASA, with the son of Dr. Hynek, looking into a case where two of the witnesses were kids at the time but were re-interviewed when they decided to come clean with their testimony in later life, and one of them is still fortunately alive. And we have found correlations now from other testimony, from people who found their own traces at the site and so on. So yes, in that particular case — I've written a book called Trinity about the case — there is no question it happened. And certainly the same thing with Socorro, and the same thing with Valensole, although those were not crashes, but there was considerable data left behind at the site.
